posts.title: Crypto rebounds as inflation stays firm; portfolio value recovers
posts.excerpt: Bitcoin traded around $77,300, up 0.7% over 24 hours, while ether rose 3.2% to roughly $2,534 in CoinGecko's price summaries. The broader market was recovering, with total crypto capitalization near $2.74 trillion. Ether outperformed bitcoin, although bitcoin remained about 2.9% lower over the week. Its roughly $76,400 to $79,600 daily range shows how much movement sits behind the modest net gain.

posts.title: Crypto declines as inflation rises; ARC weighs on portfolio
posts.excerpt: Bitcoin traded just below $77,000, down nearly 2% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell roughly 2% to about $2,445 in CoinDesk's market report. Selling was widespread: the CoinDesk 20 lost about 3%, and 95 of the CoinDesk 100 constituents declined. Zcash dropped around 12% and Hyperliquid's HYPE about 7%. The weakness coincided with rising bond yields and renewed inflation concerns, leaving smaller tokens under heavier pressure than bitcoin.

posts.title: Crypto market slips as ARC lifts portfolio value
posts.excerpt: Bitcoin traded around $78,040, down 1% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell 1.5% to roughly $2,458. CoinGabbar's CoinGecko-based market report put total crypto capitalization at $2.76 trillion, down 0.9%, with DeFi dropping 3.8%. The pullback extended beyond the two largest assets, though losses were uneven across sectors. Arbitrum's ARB fell 8.2%, illustrating the sharper losses in parts of the altcoin market.

posts.title: Crypto rebounds as oil tops $100; portfolio reaches $120,580
posts.excerpt: Bitcoin traded around $79,500, up 2.0% over 24 hours, while ether reached roughly $2,516, up 2.3%. The recovery extended beyond the two largest assets: the CoinDesk 20 index was higher, with XRP and Solana also gaining. Crypto was holding up better than European equities despite renewed pressure from energy markets. That divergence describes the session; it does not establish that geopolitical stress caused the crypto rally.
